items.topic: Fivefold prakriyā and malas as knots
items.gist: The teacher begins the identity-giving procedure over five elements, placing the three malas as knots in arm, throat, and crown.
A triple thread is arranged to express the threefold nature, and tattvas are purified in fire in their common form.
Māyā-śakti is invoked and worshipped, with specified mantras for invocation, knowledge, and action.
Invocation is identified with awakening, and fullness is established through the fourth-case ending and praise.
The supreme object of worship is independent consciousness and cannot be made manifest by ordinary means.
The formula 'I invoke the deity' displays independence, while praise and oblation establish fullness.
When the action-word is used, the guru performs abhyūhana to reveal the unmanifest object.
The disciple is struck at the tattva places, then united with the teacher through the heart and saṃhāra mudrā.
The disciple is re-embodied in māyā and undergoes saṃskāras of birth, enjoyment, and dissolution.
Fifteen mantras are assigned to the four saṃskāras, with offerings for garbhādhāna, birth, enjoyment, and bond-cutting.
The earth-tattva lord is invoked and worshipped, and the five adhvans are purified with offerings.

items.topic: Single pure alternative and final māyā
items.gist: If one pure tattva is contemplated, purification is done without separate rites, ending with final māyā worship and dismissal.
